reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,200-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-07), with the surge onset coinciding with manual-read route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts in Aug-Sep (E-01). Missed manual reads trigger estimate substitution in the billing-import step of the meter-to-cash process, and estimated bills are a documented driver of disputes (1,240 of 3,025 disputed bills, 41%, are ESTIMATED-read, E-03), making the manual-read route-completion shortfall the best-evidenced contributing cause of the dispute surge among the hypotheses tested. This mechanism does not account for the ACTUAL-read majority of disputed bills (59%, E-03), which remains an open question, and ticket response times are already within the 3.0-day SLA (E-02), ruling out the requester's response-automation framing as the fix.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,180-1,260/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-07). The surge traces to billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-11), which compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history; firmware v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report register values in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-12), causing BV-17 to misflag their reads as high-consumption anomalies and reject them at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION. This mechanism accounts for 1,184 of the 1,240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (the remaining 56 had no AMI read received at all), with billing substituting estimates for these rejected/missing reads, producing bills customers dispute (E-10). This explains the ESTIMATED-read portion (41%) of disputes but not the ACTUAL-read majority (59%, E-03), which remains open.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
